question: A 28-year-old man presents for a pre-placement health check-up. Auscultation reveals a mid-systolic click. An echocardiogram reveals a floppy mitral valve and a dilated aortic root. An ocular examination finds a subluxated lens superior and laterally. What is the most likely genetic defect?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Floppy mitral valve and dilated aortic root" -> "Subluxated lens" -> "Marfan syndrome" -> "Fibrillin" -> 95% CHAIN: "Mid-systolic click" -> "Floppy mitral valve" -> "Marfan syndrome" -> "Fibrillin" -> 90% CHAIN: "Subluxated lens" -> "Marfan syndrome" -> "Fibrillin" -> 95%
enhanced_information: The most likely genetic defect in this case is a mutation in the Fibrillin gene, associated with Marfan syndrome. The presence of a floppy mitral valve, dilated aortic root, mid-systolic click, and subluxated lens are all consistent with the manifestations of Marfan syndrome, which is linked to mutations in the Fibrillin gene.
analysis: The constellation of findings including a floppy mitral valve, dilated aortic root, mid-systolic click, and subluxated lens is highly suggestive of Marfan syndrome. Marfan syndrome is primarily caused by mutations in the Fibrillin gene. The enhanced information provided aligns with the standard medical knowledge regarding the genetic defect associated with Marfan syndrome.
